topic.title: Learning in Auctions and Strategic Markets
topic.overview: Market learning involves prices, bids, budgets, and participants whose behavior changes in response to the mechanism. The represented work studies repeated auctions, strategic buyers, coordinated bidding, and selling data with diminishing returns. Unlike ordinary prediction, an algorithm’s decisions can alter the observations it later receives.
topic.whyItMatters: A good short-term price can undermine long-term learning when buyers act strategically. Budget and incentive constraints also change what regret or economic efficiency means, so guarantees must specify feedback and participant behavior.
topic.evolution: The collection includes early advertising allocation and auction-price modeling. Later theory analyzes repeated posted prices and contextual mechanisms, while recent work handles budgeted first-price bidding and data as a continuously allocated digital good. These examples expand the market settings studied rather than establishing a universal auction rule.
openQuestions: Which learning guarantees survive strategic adaptation by multiple participants?
How should mechanisms balance data-production costs with uncertain future demand?

papers.title: Learning Personalized Ad Impact via Contextual Reinforcement Learning under Delayed Rewards
papers.tldr: A contextual reinforcement learning framework models delayed and cumulative advertising effects to learn personalized bidding strategies with a near-optimal regret bound.

papers.title: Learning to price with resource constraints: from full information to machine-learned prices
papers.tldr: Three pricing algorithms provide regret guarantees tailored to full demand knowledge, no prior information, or machine-learned prices with known error bounds.

papers.title: Mechanism Design via the Interim Relaxation
papers.tldr: An interim relaxation and two-level contention resolution framework yield revenue-approximation mechanisms under a broader range of allocation constraints.

papers.title: Multidimensional Bayesian Utility Maximization: Tight Approximations to Welfare
papers.tldr: Under i.i.d. unit-demand values, the paper gives simple prior-independent utility mechanisms with tight welfare-approximation guarantees.

papers.title: No-Regret Online Autobidding Algorithms in First-price Auctions
papers.tldr: The paper gives no-regret bidding algorithms for ROI-constrained first-price auctions against the best randomized strategy in hindsight.

papers.title: Online Bilateral Trade With Minimal Feedback: Don’t Waste Seller’s Time
papers.tldr: Querying sellers only after buyer acceptance achieves the optimal regret rate under independent valuations with bounded densities.

papers.title: Online Learning in the Repeated Mediated Newsvendor Problem
papers.tldr: The paper derives sharp regret guarantees for repeated mediated pricing under assumptions whose relaxation makes the studied problem unlearnable.

papers.title: Procurement Auctions with Predictions: Improved Frugality for Facility Location
papers.tldr: Predictions of facility-owner costs can reduce truthful-auction payments while retaining worst-case safeguards.

papers.title: Replicable Online pricing
papers.tldr: The paper develops nearly optimal replicable pricing with iterated-logarithmic sample dependence and proves that this dependence is necessary.

papers.title: Robust Contextual Pricing
papers.tldr: A black-box reduction improves regret for corrupted contextual pricing, while a lower bound rules out a purely additive corruption penalty of the proposed form.

papers.title: Smooth Quadratic Prediction Markets
papers.tldr: Smooth Quadratic Prediction Markets connect trading to gradient descent while improving a worst-case loss guarantee and preserving key market properties.

papers.title: Truthful Aggregation of LLMs with an Application to Online Advertising
papers.tldr: MOSAIC uses an auction to truthfully aggregate advertiser preferences over LLM replies without model fine-tuning or weight access.

papers.title: A Stronger Benchmark for Online Bilateral Trade: From Fixed Prices to Distributions
papers.tldr: An algorithm learns globally budget-balanced trading strategies with sublinear regret under bounded-density stochastic valuations and one-bit feedback.

papers.title: Autobidding Auctions with LLM-Powered Creatives
papers.tldr: The paper jointly models costly LLM creative enhancement and automated bidding, improving auction outcomes over tested heuristic approaches.

papers.title: Budget-Feasible Mechanisms for Submodular Welfare Maximization in Procurement Auctions
papers.tldr: BFM-SWM provides budget-feasible procurement with welfare approximation guarantees, while a valuation variant improves approximation and running time.

papers.title: Computational Arbitrage in AI Model Markets
papers.tldr: Allocating inference across competing providers can generate arbitrage profits while lowering customer prices and changing model-market competition.

papers.title: DRIVE: Distributional and Retrieval-Augmented Bidding with Value Evaluation
papers.tldr: DRIVE improves offline bidding by generating diverse and retrieved candidate bids, then selecting among them using value estimates.

papers.title: Efficient Distributionally Robust Assortment Optimization in MNL Bandits
papers.tldr: The paper develops polynomial-time algorithms and sample complexity bounds for robust assortment optimization under three distributional uncertainty measures.

papers.title: Enhancing Affine Maximizer Auctions with Correlation-Aware Payment
papers.tldr: Correlation-aware payments expand affine maximizer auctions’ revenue potential while preserving dominant-strategy truthfulness.

papers.title: Envy-Free Allocation of Indivisible Goods via Noisy Queries
papers.tldr: For two agents with bounded valuations and Gaussian query noise, the paper characterizes optimal envy-free allocation query complexity in a specified regime.

papers.title: Equilibrium Pricing in Oligopolistic Data Markets
papers.tldr: Flexible convex pricing can guarantee approximate stability against uniform-price deviations in data markets where uniform pricing need not admit equilibrium.

papers.title: From Welfare to Utility: Generalized Objectives in Budget-Feasible Procurement
papers.tldr: The paper designs budget-feasible purchasing mechanisms for welfare and buyer utility, with guarantees that depend on the objective and available cost information.

papers.title: How to Price Data: A Market Equilibrium Based Approach
papers.tldr: A Nash-based data-pricing framework yields strong guarantees for complementary-data utilities, while equilibrium can fail for substitutable-data utilities.

papers.title: Model Monotonicity in Autobidding Auctions: When Do Better Predictions Lead to Better Outcomes?
papers.tldr: Better advertising predictions improve auction outcomes only under particular combinations of auction format, bidder behavior, and budget constraints.

papers.title: On the Coordination of Value-Maximizing Bidders
papers.tldr: Allowing only the highest-value coordinated bidder to compete improves group value and Return-on-Spend compliance for a broad class of auto-bidding algorithms.

papers.title: Revenue Guarantees of No-Swap-Regret Dynamics in First Price Auctions
papers.tldr: The paper bounds first-price auction revenue near the second-highest valuation and derives polynomial convergence rates for no-swap-regret bidders.

papers.title: Revisiting the Bertrand Paradox via Equilibrium Analysis of No-regret Learners
papers.tldr: The paper analyzes how external-regret and swap-regret learning shape equilibria in a repeated discrete Bertrand pricing game.

papers.title: Risk-Averse and Optimistic Advertiser Incentive Compatibility in Auto-bidding
papers.tldr: Second-price auctions satisfy two relaxed truthfulness criteria that compare equilibrium outcomes from risk-averse or optimistic advertiser perspectives.

papers.title: Robust and Consistent Ski Rental with Distributional Advice
papers.tldr: Distribution-aware ski rental algorithms improve performance with accurate advice while retaining explicit robustness guarantees against prediction errors.

papers.title: Selling Data as a Digital Good with Scaling Valuations
papers.tldr: Under scaling-law valuations, adaptive production and simple trading mechanisms achieve provable approximation guarantees for selling continuous quantities of data.

papers.title: The (Marginal) Value of a Search Ad: An Online Causal Framework for Repeated Second-price Auctions
papers.tldr: A causal bidding framework learns the incremental value of search ads and exploits second-price payments to achieve rate-optimal regret.

papers.title: Welfare-Optimal Classification with Accuracy Auctions
papers.tldr: A truthful auction lets a classifier optimize users’ benefits from correct predictions while accounting for privately held valuations.
